subject: Nimbus Health trial: goals, timelines, and risk owners
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@nimbushealth.com>, Clara Li <clara.li@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nimbus trial: post-call recap and proposed success criteria

Hi Sanjay / Clara —

Thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and our proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the pilot: 

1) Trial scope and goal
- Scope: 2-week trial focused on inpatient discharge summary generation for the Cardiology unit (approx. 250 records/day).
- Primary success metric: precision@90 for clinical-problem extraction and <10% manual edits on final summaries.
- Secondary: median generation latency <400ms for 512-token prompts.

2) Evaluation plan / ownership
- Nimbus team will provide sample de-identified dataset + schema (owner: Clara). See attached data map.
- Redwood will run baseline runs, provide eval dashboard and example failures (owner: Kimberly).
- Acceptance: mutual sign-off on sample set and evaluation notebook.

3) Timeline
- Receive sample data (target): Tue 2027-03-23
- Baseline runs and initial report: Thu 2027-03-25
- Iteration window and checkpoints: 3/25–3/30
- Decision/rollout recommendation: Wed 2027-03-31

4) Risks flagged now
- Data format mismatch (CSV vs HL7) — mitigation: mapping template (Dev).
- PHI/inference policy questions — mitigation: sign-off on de-identification & earliest legal review.

Attachments: 2027-03-21-nimbus-trial-success-metrics.xlsx (proposed metrics), nimbus-poc-data-map.pdf

Next steps: Clara to share sample export; Dev and I will validate schema and confirm baseline run window. 

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0192

--
Note: Redwood pilot instances run with a default isolation policy; if Nimbus needs VPC-only, flag it in reply so we add Private deployment checks.
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Nimbus trial: post-call recap and proposed success criteria

Got it. A couple of technical clarifications I want to capture before Clara sends data: 

- Preferred export format: ask for compressed JSONL with fields: patient_id (hashed), encounter_id, discharge_notes, structured_problem_list. If they only have CSV we can map but need the header mapping up front.
- Tokenization: we should set a strict 1024 token cap for initial runs and return truncation stats.
- KV-cache warmup: request they provide a 2-day historical slice for warmup so we can simulate prefix caching.

I'll draft a short data schema email snippet Kimberly can paste to Clara. Also, I'll prepare a minimal mapping script and attach it once data arrives.

Dev
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Clara Li <clara.li@nimbushealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Nimbus trial: post-call recap and proposed success criteria

Hi Kimberly / Dev —

Thanks — we're aligned on the goals. We've attached a de-identified JSONL export (sent via secure Drive link) and a short data dictionary. A few notes/questions from our side: 

- We have two export options: CSV with HL7-style fields or de-id JSONL. We will prioritize the JSONL export tomorrow (3/23).
- Is there a recommended sample size? We can send 1 week (approx. 1,750 records) or 2 weeks. Clara prefers 2 weeks for better signal.
- On latency: 400ms median is fine; are there trade-offs if we enable 8-bit quantization?

We'll upload to the Drive folder you shared by EOD 3/23.

Clara
Data Integration Lead, Nimbus Health
clara.li@nimbushealth.com

On Tue, Mar 23, 2027 at 09:12 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks — 2 weeks sounds good. Clara, please include a short sample mapping if you pick CSV. Dev, I'll loop security once we confirm de-id approach.
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 16:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Nimbus trial - blocker discovered & escalation plan

Heads up — after a quick validation of the JSONL sample (Clara delivered part of the folder this morning), Dev found a schema inconsistency that will block baseline runs until tomorrow morning: the encounter_id field is sometimes an integer and sometimes encoded as "enc1234" string in the sample.

Impact: baseline run cannot be completed today; may push initial report to Fri 3/26 if mapping required.

Proposed mitigation and owners:
- Immediate: Dev will run a normalization pass (script attached) to coerce encounter_id to string and emit mapping report (owner: Dev) — ETA: 12 hours.
- If mapping reveals missing keys (e.g., discharge_notes null for ~>5% of records), we escalate to Clara for data re-extract (owner: Clara) — SLA: 24 hours.
- Escalation path: if data re-extract not possible within SLA, Kimberly to escalate to Sanjay and sales leadership to request extended window or accept smaller sample.

Attachments: data-normalize-encounterid.py (script stub) — note: script uses a safe coercion and logs ambiguous rows to a csv: ambiguous_encounters.csv

Next steps: I'll confirm after Dev completes the normalization run. If we still see >5% nulls in discharge_notes, I'll open an escalation and propose shifting the decision date to 3/31.

Thanks,

Kimberly
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

On Wed, Mar 24, 2027 at 08:45 AM Clara Li <clara.li@nimbushealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the heads up — I will ask our ETL team to prioritize re-extract if you hit the null threshold.
